task: score the NUAA test frames of each fold with the 36 patience-4 checkpoints of run 20261106-SESSABLRUN-d999458, before and after re-estimating the moving statistics of their five BatchNormalization layers on the fitting set of their arm and fold with the estimator of PR #27 (scripts/nuaa_bn_recalibration.py, unchanged, SHA-256 pinned), on in-memory copies; compare APCER, BPCER and ACER at the fixed threshold 0.5 and AUROC per model, for the whole test of the fold and for session 03, with paired summaries and a subject bootstrap; no training, no trained parameter changed, no .keras file written
authorisation: coordinator, C2 card, 16 November 2026 (after merging PR #27): verify on the NUAA test of the same 36 checkpoints, without new training, whether the effect of the BN recalibration holds; checkpoints, split, preprocessing and the estimator of PR #27 unchanged, recalibration only on the fitting set of the model's arm and fold, on copies, trained parameters unchanged, all 36 models included, also those worsened on the dev; before/after on the same test frames (APCER, BPCER, ACER at the fixed threshold 0.5, AUROC) by arm, fold and seed, whole test and session 03 separately, with counts, per-subject results and every worsening, and paired summaries with subject-level uncertainty; before the run, a short note, the configuration and the code in a new pull request towards research/pad-2026 (planned comparisons, baseline checks, tolerances, estimated time within 4 CPU hours); once the checks pass, the run may proceed without a further approval; on a baseline discrepancy, stop and document it; no change of the procedure based on the test results; to be stated as a post hoc diagnostic extension on an already analysed test, not an independent validation

declarations.post_hoc: post hoc diagnostic extension on a test already analysed: the before metrics of these 36 checkpoints on this test are already published (parent run 20261106-SESSABLRUN-d999458), and the re-estimation was chosen and its effect first measured on the dev of the same folds (PR #27); this is not an independent validation
declarations.threshold: the decision threshold is fixed at 0.5 (attack if score_attack > 0.5, tie = bona fide); no threshold is selected or re-selected, on the dev or on the test; AUROC is threshold-free
declarations.procedure: the procedure, the tolerances, the reading rule and the outputs are fixed in this configuration and in the note before the run and are not changed after any test result is seen; every outcome is reported
declarations.cause: no statement on the cause of the dev saturation: every reading is limited to the effect of this re-estimation on these checkpoints on this test, at the fixed threshold 0.5 for APCER, BPCER and ACER (AUROC is threshold-free)
declarations.worsening: all 36 models are included, among them the 17 with a dev or fitting indicator worsened in PR #27, marked in results.csv (column dev_worsened) and, in aggregate.md, in the table of all models and in the list of worsenings; every model and scope whose ACER, APCER or BPCER is higher, or whose AUROC is lower, after the re-estimation is listed with its size, however small

parent_run.used: status.json, the public and restricted SHA256SUMS, the public aggregate.json only as bytes for its SHA-256 (never parsed: it holds the published test metrics), and per model card.json, dev_scores.csv, threshold.json, LivenessNet.keras and test_scores.csv: the <model>_test_scores.csv files are hashed in phase 0 against the restricted SHA256SUMS, parsed in phase 1 for the test baseline and used again in phase 3b as a reported check of the before metrics; the fold schema of the parent configuration is loaded with its test manifests (fold<k>_test.csv); the fitting, dev and test frames come from the same cell manifests, fold manifests, cache and extracted frames as in the parent run; of the folds run only status.json, the restricted SHA256SUMS and extracted_frames.csv (no public file opened). Every other key of this section is equal to the PR #27 configuration by rule; this key is rewritten for this run

bnrecal_run.used: status.json; the public and restricted SHA256SUMS; public results.csv (groups and dev worsening flags) and run_record.json (code_sha256); restricted public_SHA256SUMS.sha256 and, per model, _scores.csv (the dev rows with statistics re-estimated) and _bn_statistics.json (the installed float32 statistics); every file equal to its SHA256SUMS line

architecture.name: LivenessNet
architecture.augmentation: none inside the saved model: LivenessNet (src/architectures.py) has no augmentation, rescaling or preprocessing layer; the trainer's augmentation (nuaa_folds_run.default_trainer: RandomFlip, RandomRotation, RandomZoom, RandomTranslation, RandomBrightness, RandomContrast, GaussianNoise) is a separate tf.keras.Sequential mapped on the training dataset and is not saved; the runner refuses a saved model whose layers (names and classes, in order) differ from this list

batchnorm.inference: y = gamma (x - moving_mean) / sqrt(moving_variance + epsilon) + beta, per channel (Keras 2.15, training=False)
batchnorm.running_variance_in_training: recorded fact, not used: during training Keras 2.15 updated the moving variance with the Bessel-corrected batch variance for the four convolutional layers (fused kernel, factor n/(n-1), n = 16 x H x W) and with the biased batch variance for bn_dense; the population variance chosen here differs from an N/(N-1) version by the relative factor 1/(N-1): at most 1/933 for bn_dense (934 frames) and less than 1e-7 for the convolutional layers (N >= 934 x 128 x 128)

estimator.statistics: for each BatchNormalization layer, the per-channel global mean and variance of the layer INPUT over the whole fitting set of the model's arm and fold (1,400 frames for B and A*, 934 for B')
estimator.order: layer by layer in network order (bn1_1, bn1_2, bn2_1, bn2_2, bn_dense): the input of a layer is computed with the earlier layers already carrying their re-estimated statistics (one pass over the fitting set per layer)
estimator.mode: inference mode (training=False): dropout inactive, BatchNormalization layers with their moving statistics; no augmentation (frames / 255 as in scoring)
estimator.counts: values per channel: frames x H x W for the four convolutional layers (256 x 256 for bn1_1 and bn1_2, 128 x 128 for bn2_1 and bn2_2), frames for bn_dense; batches of 16, the last one shorter (1,400 = 87 x 16 + 8; 934 = 58 x 16 + 6) and weighted by its own count; the accumulated count is checked against frames x H x W
estimator.variance: population variance (divisor N) from the exact union of the batches in float64 (Chan et al.: per batch count, mean and sum of squared deviations), equal to sum of squares / N - mean^2 and to sum_b n_b (var_b + (mean_b - mean)^2) / N over the concatenated values, without the cancellation of the first form; not the mean of the batch variances, not the unweighted mean of the batch means
estimator.cast: float32, round to nearest (numpy astype) of the float64 result; the float64 values are kept in the restricted statistics file
estimator.copy: an in-memory copy (clone_model and set_weights) of the checkpoint loaded from the parent file, SHA-256 verified just before loading; the file is never opened for writing and no recalibrated .keras is saved (the copy is reproducible from the statistics file); after the five layers every weight tensor of the copy is compared byte for byte with the original: exactly the 10 moving tensors differ, each equal to the installed float32 statistic, and every other tensor (kernels, biases, gamma, beta) is bit-identical; otherwise FAIL
estimator.consistency: one multi-output pass over the fitting set with the final copy: the per-channel moments of the input of each BatchNormalization layer, recomputed with all five layers re-estimated, must equal the installed moving_mean and moving_variance within consistency_rel x |recomputed| + consistency_abs; a channel outside is an implementation failure (FAIL, no reading); the same pass gives the fitting accuracy and loss after

evaluation.input: frames / 255 in float32, assembled in key order as in the parent run
evaluation.mode: inference (training=False), checkpoint loaded with compile=False as in the parent scorer
evaluation.probability: softmax output of the layer output, column 1 (attack), from the evaluator of nuaa_bn_recalibration (BR.evaluate) on the dev and on the test; in the baseline the parent's own scorer (nuaa_folds_run.tf_scorer on the file) is also run on the dev, not on the test. Every other key of this section is equal to the PR #27 configuration by rule; this key is rewritten for this run
evaluation.logits: z = h @ W + b in float64 from the input of the layer output (as tf_logits of the parent runner)
evaluation.val_loss: mean categorical cross-entropy from the logits as Keras 2.15 (logsumexp(z) - z[y], no clipping: nuaa_session_ablation_run.val_loss_logits); the same unweighted formula for the fitting loss
evaluation.accuracy: argmax of the probabilities against the label (Keras CategoricalAccuracy, tie = index 0), correct / n in float32; the accuracy at the 0.5 decision is also reported
evaluation.auroc: Mann-Whitney AUROC of the attack score, attack positive, ties 0.5 (nuaa_folds_run.auroc)
evaluation.decision: attack if score_attack > 0.5, tie = bona fide (for the discordant-decision check)

recovery_criterion.text: dev accuracy >= 0.75 and val_loss < 1.0 (val_loss from the logits); the same thresholds read on the fitting set in inference mode (accuracy and unweighted loss)
recovery_criterion.source: recovery criterion of the degenerate study (research/nuaa-degenerate-trainings/NOTE.md)

degenerate.source: degenerate criterion of the degenerate study 20261107-DEGEN-a3b4dc0, applied to the parent cards

ten.definition: the degenerate checkpoints: restored epoch 1 or 2 with dev accuracy 0.5 (within 1e-6) in the parent card

apart.definition: not degenerate and outside the recovery criterion at its checkpoint (parent card): reported apart, not deciding

control.definition: every other checkpoint: not degenerate and meeting the recovery criterion at its checkpoint

dev_worsened.definition: models with at least one worsening flag on the dev or the fitting in the public results.csv of the BNRECAL run (lost_criterion, dev_accuracy_lower, val_loss_higher, dev_auroc_lower, fitting_accuracy_lower or fitting_loss_higher); included like every other model and marked in the tables
dev_worsened.source: results/bnrecal/20261114-BNRECAL-a10a082/public/results.csv, derived by the runner and compared with this list

dev_probability_max_abs_diff.source: the tolerance of the coordinator's R2 replication package (1e-5 absolute, no discordant decision), used in the C1 crop check (research/c1-crop-check/README.md): there scores stored on the GPU one image at a time were reproduced within 8.9e-8 in those conditions and within 2.9e-6 on the CPU in batches of 16; here stored scores and baseline share file, CPU and batch 16; not measured before the run, since no inference precedes it; applied to the parent's scorer and to the evaluator of this script, frame by frame against the stored dev scores

dev_decisions_discordant_at_0_5.source: same R2 criterion: no decision at 0.5 may change; measured on the stored files without inference: no stored dev score of the 36 models lies within 1e-3 of 0.5 (closest 1.03e-3)

val_loss_abs.source: the absolute part of the parent runner's check (nuaa_folds_run.VAL_LOSS_TOL); its alternative 1 % branch is not used, since 1 % of the largest recorded value, 60.9868, is 0.61; measured on the stored cards without inference, the val_loss recomputed by the parent runner at run time differs from best_val_loss by at most 2.9e-6 absolute (arm_a_star_fold2_seed44, recorded 18.0934) and 2.5e-5 relative (arm_a_star_fold2_seed42, absolute 2.7e-9), two different models; the difference from val_loss_recomputed is reported, not binding

dev_accuracy_abs.source: the same number of correct dev frames (one frame = 0.0025 of 400; val_acc_at_best is the float32 of k/400); measured on the stored files without inference: the accuracy of the stored dev scores at the 0.5 decision equals val_acc_at_best for 36 of 36 models (difference 0 in float32)

softmax_of_logits_max_abs_diff.source: PROB_TOL of the parent runner (softmax of the float64 logits against the float32 probabilities); the same bound holds after the recalibration, on the dev and on the fitting, where a failure stops the run (FAIL)

consistency_rel.source: implementation check, not a baseline: the moments of the input of a layer depend only on the earlier layers, which are not changed after it, so the recomputed moments differ from the installed ones only by the float32 cast (relative 6e-8) and by the order of the float32 operations of the forward pass; 1e-4 relative is about 1,700 times the cast error and far below any change that would matter after normalisation

consistency_abs.source: absolute floor for channels whose mean or variance is zero or near zero (dead ReLU channels): 1e-6 is one thousandth of epsilon (0.001), which bounds the normalising denominator from below

test_probability_max_abs_diff.source: the dev tolerance of PR #27 (the coordinator's R2 replication package: 1e-5 absolute, no discordant decision), applied frame by frame to the attack probability of the evaluator of nuaa_bn_recalibration (CPU, batch 16, frames / 255, inference mode) against the parent's stored <model>_test_scores.csv, produced by the parent's scorer from the same checkpoint file on the CPU in batches of 16; in the BNRECAL baseline the same evaluator reproduced the stored dev scores with largest difference 0 for 36 of 36 models (its public baseline.csv); not measured on the test, since no test inference precedes the run

test_decisions_discordant_at_0_5.source: same R2 criterion: no decision at 0.5 may change (decision rule of the project: attack if score > 0.5, tie = bona fide); the distance of the stored test scores from 0.5 is not known before the run, since their content is not opened before it

recalibration_statistics_rel.source: the consistency tolerance of PR #27 (consistency_rel): the same code, frames, CPU and batch should give the same float32 statistics as the BNRECAL run; bit-identical statistics are expected but not assumed: the largest difference and whether the 10 tensors are bit-identical are reported per model

recalibration_statistics_abs.source: the consistency tolerance of PR #27 (consistency_abs), absolute floor for statistics at or near zero

recalibration_dev_probability_max_abs_di.source: the same R2 criterion, applied to the dev probabilities after the re-estimation against the BNRECAL dev scores with statistics re-estimated

recalibration_dev_decisions_discordant_a.source: same R2 criterion: no dev decision at 0.5 after the re-estimation may differ from the BNRECAL run

stop_rules.fail: FAIL (exit 1): every output in public/ and restricted/ is removed; status.json keeps the reason and run.log the lines printed until the error; those lines hold test metrics only if the error happens in phase 3b or in the final writes (phases 1, 2 and 3a print no test metric)
stop_rules.baseline: phase 1, before any re-estimation: if any check fails for at least one of the 36 models (dev checks of PR #27; test frames aligned with the stored test scores; test probability difference; discordant decisions at 0.5; softmax of the logits), the run stops with status BASELINE_FAILED (exit 3) after checking all 36, writes public/baseline.csv with every value, reference, difference and tolerance, and computes nothing after it; no re-estimated statistic and no test metric. An error that prevents the evaluation itself (unexpected architecture, non-finite output, SHA-256 mismatch, unreadable or non-numeric stored scores) is a FAIL with its reason in status.json and no table
stop_rules.recalibration: phase 2, before any test score with re-estimated statistics: if the installed statistics or the dev probabilities after the re-estimation differ from those of the BNRECAL run beyond the tolerances for at least one of the 36 models, the run stops with status RECALIBRATION_MISMATCH (exit 4) after checking all 36, writes public/recalibration_check.csv with the differences, and computes or writes no test score with re-estimated statistics. A failure of the checks of PR #27 inside the re-estimation (a trained tensor changed, consistency outside tolerance, softmax of the logits) is a FAIL

comparison.decision: attack if score_attack > threshold (tie = bona fide)
comparison.frames: the test frames of the model's fold: every frame of the held-out subjects listed in fold<k>_test.csv of the fold schema (test_frames_per_fold, checked by the runner; an empty fold is refused), assembled in key order from the cache and the extracted frames as in the parent run (phase 1) and reassembled with the same keys (phase 3a); the same frames before and after; scope test = all of them, scope session_03 = those with session 03
comparison.auroc: Mann-Whitney AUROC of the attack score, attack positive, ties 0.5 (nuaa_folds_run.auroc through nuaa_folds_run.stratum_metrics)
comparison.undefined: a metric of a scope where a class is absent is reported as not defined (NA), never dropped: its difference and its worsening flag are NA, a summary with an undefined model has no mean and no reading for that metric, and every undefined case is listed in aggregate.md
comparison.worsening: per model and scope: acer_higher, apcer_higher, bpcer_higher (value after > value before) and auroc_lower (after < before); any change in that direction counts, however small; every case is listed in aggregate.md with before, after and difference
comparison.per_subject: per model, scope, statistics and held-out subject: counts, rejected bona fide and accepted attacks at 0.5, APCER, BPCER, ACER and AUROC, in the restricted per_subject.csv only (the public files carry no subject identifier, as in the parent run)

bootstrap.recipe: the resampling of the project, unchanged (nuaa_session_ablation_run: SR.BOOT, SR.boot_picks, SR.subject_stats, SR.weighted_metrics, SR.interval; SR.BOOT_RECIPE): generator numpy.random.default_rng(0) (PCG64), restarted for every summary and scope; the held-out subjects of the scope of the folds of the summary's models, pooled and in ascending identifier order (16 on the whole test when the summary covers the four folds; in session_03 the subjects with frames in that scope); at every resample integers(0, n, n); every model's metrics computed from the multiplicities of the subjects of its own fold (per-subject counts and pairwise Mann-Whitney counts, identical to recomputing them on the frames); the same resampled subjects for before and after, for every model of the summary and for every metric; percentiles 2.5 and 97.5 with np.percentile, linear interpolation; no interval with fewer than 5 held-out subjects (so the model apart, one fold with four subjects, has none); summary.csv gives per summary and scope the held-out subjects, those with bona fide frames, those with attack frames, and the valid resamples
bootstrap.combination: new element, declared: the statistic of a resample is the mean over the models of the summary of the paired difference after - before, and a resample in which the metric of any model of the summary (before or after) is not defined does not count for that metric; dropped resamples are reported (valid_resamples), not corrected; with a single model this is the paired bootstrap of the project (SR.paired_bootstrap)

reading_rule.primary: primary: the ten degenerate checkpoints, scope test (all test frames of the fold), ACER at the fixed threshold 0.5: the mean over the ten of the paired difference after - before with its subject-bootstrap interval, read with three pre-written statements (interval entirely below zero; containing zero, a bound exactly at zero counting as containing zero; entirely above zero), or a fourth, not_available, when the metric is not defined for a model of the summary or there is no interval (fewer than 5 subjects): no reading; plus the count of the ten whose ACER is lower, equal or higher after; applied mechanically by the script
reading_rule.below: {who}, scope {scope}, {metric}: mean paired difference (after - before) {difference}, subject-bootstrap interval [{low}, {high}] entirely below zero: on this test, the effect of this re-estimation on these checkpoints is a lower mean value; a post hoc diagnostic reading, not an independent validation, and no statement on the cause of the saturation
reading_rule.contains: {who}, scope {scope}, {metric}: mean paired difference (after - before) {difference}, subject-bootstrap interval [{low}, {high}] containing zero: on this test, this interval does not show a direction of the effect of this re-estimation on these checkpoints, nor the absence of an effect; a post hoc diagnostic reading, not an independent validation
reading_rule.above: {who}, scope {scope}, {metric}: mean paired difference (after - before) {difference}, subject-bootstrap interval [{low}, {high}] entirely above zero: on this test, the effect of this re-estimation on these checkpoints is a higher mean value; a post hoc diagnostic reading, not an independent validation, and no statement on the cause of the saturation
reading_rule.count: Of the {n} degenerate checkpoints, ACER at the fixed threshold 0.5 on the whole test is lower after the re-estimation for {lower}, equal for {equal} and higher for {higher}; every model is listed in the tables
reading_rule.secondary: secondary, descriptive, no verdict beyond the same statements: session 03, the controls, the model reported apart (one fold, four held-out subjects: no interval, so not_available), all 36, the three arms, and APCER, BPCER and AUROC; for AUROC a value above zero is a higher AUROC; for APCER, BPCER and ACER a value below zero is a lower error rate
reading_rule.limits: post hoc on a test already analysed, with the before metrics published and the re-estimation chosen on the dev of the same folds; one estimator, one threshold (0.5), the restored checkpoint of each training only; the subject intervals rest on 16 held-out subjects (four per fold; 15 with bona fide and 15 with attack frames on the whole test, and in session 03 only nine with bona fide frames: 2, 3, 2 and 2 per fold); with so few clusters a percentile interval may be too narrow; resamples dropped for an undefined metric are reported, not corrected; the summaries are not independent of each other (arms and groups share models and subjects); the effect on these checkpoints on this test, not a statement on other checkpoints, other thresholds, other data or the cause of the saturation

budget.estimate: derived from the BNRECAL run 20261114-BNRECAL-a10a082 on the same machine (run.log and public run_record.json: phase 0 2.8 s, baseline 342.0 s, re-estimation and evaluation 1400.9 s, total 1748.6 s for 36 models); its baseline evaluated per model 800 dev frames (two scorers) and 1,400 or 934 fitting frames with two model loads: a least-squares line over the 36 models gives 2.05 s per model plus 0.003612 s per frame (277 frames per second; 216.6 overall). This run: phase 1, 36 x 2.05 s (two loads) + (28,800 dev + 113,526 test frames) x 0.003612 s = 588 s; phase 2, the same passes as the BNRECAL phase 2 (five re-estimation passes and one consistency pass over the fitting, one dev pass) = 1,401 s; phase 3a, 36 x 1.03 s (one load) + 113,526 x 0.003612 s = 447 s; 588 + 1,401 + 447 = 2,436 s, plus about 90 s not measured (inputs, input re-verification, metrics, bootstrap, figure and writes) = about 2,526 s, about 42 minutes. Upper estimate: the slowest measured rates, applied alike to phases 1 and 3a (168.3 frames per second including the model loads, the slowest baseline model; 48.5 s per model for the re-estimation and evaluation, the slowest model): 845 + 1,746 + 675 + 90 = 3,356 s (56 minutes), doubled for the unmeasured parts (assembling up to 3,439 test frames per model, memory) = about 112 minutes. The four-hour limit is applied as elapsed time of a CPU-only run, as in the earlier runs: a cap of 240 minutes of wall time, checked before each model (and before each layer in phase 2), never inside phase 3b, so a run can end PASS slightly after 240 minutes; the process CPU time over all threads is recorded (run_record.json, process_cpu_seconds), not capped and not estimated, and can exceed the elapsed time (several threads)
budget.on_cap_exceeded: INCOMPLETE (exit 2), in phase 1, 2 or 3a: no further model; the checks completed so far are published (baseline.csv and, from phase 2 on, recalibration_check.csv, with the run record and SHA256SUMS); no test metric is computed, logged or published, no results.csv, aggregate.json, aggregate.md, summary.csv or figure, and no per-frame test score file with re-estimated statistics is kept; phase 3b is all or nothing and does not consult the cap or the stop request (a few seconds of NumPy): a stop requested during 3b is not consulted and 3b and the final writes complete
budget.voluntary_stop: SIGUSR1 to the run's pid stops it at the next check, as INCOMPLETE

test: this run reads the test: in phase 0 it opens and validates the fold schema (fold<k>_fitting.csv, fold<k>_dev.csv and fold<k>_test.csv, as the parent run did) and hashes every <model>_test_scores.csv of the parent run against its restricted SHA256SUMS without parsing it; in phase 1 it assembles the test frames of each fold (every frame of the held-out subjects, from the cache and the extracted frames, in key order, as the parent run did), scores them with each checkpoint and its original statistics with the evaluator of nuaa_bn_recalibration (the parent's own scorer is used only on the dev) and parses the parent's <model>_test_scores.csv to compare the per-frame attack probabilities; the evaluator also computes a test accuracy and AUROC in memory, which are discarded: no test metric is written or logged in phase 1; only if phases 1 and 2 pass for all 36 models, phase 3a reassembles the same test frames and scores them with the re-estimated statistics for all 36, the 36 .keras files, the parent's restricted SHA256SUMS and the two SHA256SUMS of the BNRECAL run are re-hashed, and only then phase 3b computes the test metrics (APCER, BPCER and ACER at the fixed threshold 0.5, AUROC) before and after and, as a reported check, from the parent's stored scores; the M2 manifests official_test and cnn_test are read to index the cache; the public aggregate of the parent run, which holds test metrics already published, is read only as bytes for its SHA-256 and never parsed; no public file of the folds run is opened
